legalwise.co.za zoominfo.com/c/legalwise/429691676 LegalWise (founded 1984, Johannesburg) is South Africa's leading legal-expenses insurance provider, with 350,000+ members and 1.1 million people covered across the country. For a monthly fee starting at ~R151 ($8), members get 24/7 legal advice, court-cost coverage up to R405,000 per case, and access to a network of 220+ partner law firms — helping ordinary people afford lawyers for labour, criminal, family and municipal disputes. The company has 400–800 staff, offices in all nine provinces plus Botswana and Namibia, and handles 125,000+ consultations and ~70,000 new cases a year. It sits inside the LEGA insurance group (with insurer LEZA), where 62% was bought by black-owned investment firm Sithega in 2023 while Hollard kept 38%; group gross premiums run ~R800–850 million/year. Led by CEO Siva Gengan

samwumed.org zoominfo.com/c/samwumed/346685548 SAMWUMED (founded 1952, Cape Town) is a closed, self-administered medical aid scheme serving South African municipal workers — roughly 35,000 members and 73,000 covered lives. It collects about R1.9 billion/year in contributions, kept reserves over R1.3 billion and posted a R14.3 million surplus in 2024 (solvency 68% vs the 25% legal minimum). Plans are income-banded and cheap (from ~R750/month with a 60% employer subsidy), covering hospitals, doctors, medication, dentistry and optics. Led by Principal Officer Francina Mosoeu with a union-appointed board, it administers benefits with Medscheme across a network of private hospital groups. Key problems right now: membership shrinking ~15%/year as young people leave, and an ongoing court battle with the Melomed hospital group over contract exclusions — plus the long-term threat of national health insurance reform.

edcon.co.za zoominfo.com/c/edcon/36900910 Edcon (roots from 1929, Johannesburg) was South Africa's largest non-food retailer — owner of iconic chains Edgars, Jet, CNA and Boardmans, with ~1,200 stores across Southern Africa, ~19,000 staff, revenue of R25+ billion and four million private-label credit cards. It was crippled by Bain Capital's 2007 leveraged buyout (~R25 billion), losing market share to discounters before COVID-19 lockdown wiped out R2 billion in sales and forced business rescue in April 2020. The group was then broken up: Jet was sold to The Foschini Group (~R480m), Edgars to Retailability (~R350m, 5,200 jobs saved), CNA and credit books to other buyers. The Edcon holding company itself no longer trades — edcon.co.za is now a business-rescue notice board where practitioners Marsden and Schapiro distribute sale proceeds to creditors (payments started September 2024, proceedings still open as of 2025).

It provides offensive-security services: penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, hardening, source-code and web/API audits, mobile app audits, social-engineering tests and full Red Team engagements, working to PTES/OWASP/OSSTMM standards with manual verification. The team holds top certifications (CEH, CISSP, PMP, Checkpoint CCSE, ISO 27001) and its co-founder later moved to a senior role at the NATO Communications and Information Agency. A notable credential is its contract with Portugal's National Cybersecurity Centre (CNCS) to run the "Cidadão Ciberseguro" course for government workers on the state NAU platform.
